messages.text:
"Create a complete playable top-down 2D HTML5 Canvas + vanilla JS browser game \"Mr. Rescue: Extinguish Protocol\". Single HTML file preferred. Landscape only, canvas fills entire phone screen (viewport + resize).

CONTROLS: Dual virtual joysticks (Android-style). Left half touch = movement joystick (appears on touch, follows finger). Right half touch = aim + continuous fire joystick. Always-visible button (bottom) to cycle/select extinguisher: Water, Foam, Cryo, CO2. Show current type + ammo. Keyboard fallback (WASD + mouse + 1-4).

CORE: Top-down reimagining of Mr. Rescue. Firefighter rescues civilians (pick up/carry or escort to windows/exits/safe zones). Primary goal = rescue, not full extinguish. Heat rises near fire/hits (coolants reduce it; full heat = death). Each extinguisher has limited ammo (recharges/pickups). Fire spreads over time. Power-ups, score (rescues + efficiency). Multi-room floors, progress by rescuing then reaching stairs/exit. Pixel-art style matching original (red helmet, yellow suit, furniture, windows).

SYSTEMS: 4 extinguishers matched to 4 moving enemy types (wrong type useless or worsens): Water→Charcoal/Ember, Foam→Magma/Oil, Cryo→Frostfire, CO2→Gas Phantom/Leak. Enemies patrol/chase/spread fire/attack. Puzzle elements: path-blocking fires needing correct type, sequences, environmental uses (Cryo freezes, Water cools, CO2 suppresses gas/elec, Foam dissolves), civilians requiring right extinguisher nearby. Limited ammo + mixed enemies force planning. Aggressive enemies, spreading fire, rising heat = challenging.

UI: Heat bar, ammo, score, civilians remaining, current extinguisher. 3–5 rooms demonstrating systems. Clean code, touch multi-touch support, particles, local high-score. End of floor requires most/all civilians rescued.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
